judge_reasoning: All responses correctly identify Thèque as a traditional Norman bat-and-ball game with batting/running to score and a fielding side trying to stop runners. Candidate [3] is best overall because it includes distinctive Thèque elements (central stake and bases as ground holes) while maintaining a coherent gameplay description, even though some specifics like origin date/player count are uncertain. Candidate [1] is slightly more generic and omits those distinctive elements, while [2] introduces a pitcher (which is not supported by the other responses’ framing and is likely inaccurate). Candidate [4] adds many highly specific claims (field shape, ball type, “semestres,” player count), which are mostly unverifiable here and reduce reliability.
